note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

compliance.verdict: The packaging of the item is compliant, but its V6 oracle checks less than the instruction asks. Confirmed points: the split is right (blocks/peak_detector2.grc is a test seed, task split test, id and dir match). The licence, source, sha256 (78cb5456...) and cluster_id are correct, and the provenance, review and fault fields are present. The seven 'original' values in the perturbation record match the example file. The canary GUID appears only in task.json. Disjointness holds: no training-side spec involves peak detection. Running build.py again in scratch gives byte-identical task.json, reference.grc, start.grc and variants. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates and got the same gates.json: solvability 10/10, 433 tokens, 3/3 variants reach V6, start first fails at V3 with the stated type and size mismatch, 13/13 mutants are valid with kill rate 1.0. The weaknesses are in the oracle. The +-2 % peak-count tolerance accepts flowgraphs with spurious peaks, including one that only restores the example's original look-ahead (F1, medium). Peak position ('top of every ramp') is never checked, so a delayed indicator passes (F2). 'Keep the Peak Detector2 settings' is not enforced (F3; the author already flagged it). The p2p group cannot be pass-to-pass when the start fails at V3 (F4). Tightening the count and adding an equal_prefix position check would fix F1 and F2. I did not edit the task; the only write was the gate re-run rewriting gates.json, which came out identical to the original.

findings.claim: The peak_rate tolerance of +-2 % is looser than the spec. The instruction asks for 'exactly one detected peak per sawtooth period', and the reference count has no run-to-run noise, yet the oracle accepts flowgraphs that flag extra peaks that are not ramp tops.
findings.evidence: I probed with ladder.check plus an extra edge tap on the sawtooth (scratch script scratchpad/gbf09/probe.py, outputs in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-09). The reference, v1, v2, v3, and the reference with maxoutbuf 7 or 64 on the source and detector all give exactly 192 flags in the 15360-sample window (mean 0.0125, every flag at a ramp top). I then changed only the look-ahead back to the example's original formula int(samp_rate/1e3/1.1), which is 43 at 48 kHz. That gives 194 flags in the window: mean 0.01263 (+1.04 %), rms 0.112384, peak spacings from 4 to 58 samples, and 3.3 % of flags not at a ramp top. It passes all 5 V6 checks. Look-ahead 50 gives 193 flags and also passes. Look-ahead 40 (198 flags) and 81 (186 flags) are the first values that fail. +-2 % of 192 means up to 3 spurious or missing peaks are accepted. This answer also partly restores the memorised example value, which the perturbation was meant to catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the count exact, as the spec says. Tighten the peak_rate mean check to rel_tol of about 0.003 (less than half a peak in 192). Then the rms check is also effectively exact, or it can be removed as redundant. Add a mutation {op: set_param, block: lookahead, param: value, value: 'int(samp_rate/1e3/1.1)', breaks: peak_rate} so the mutation gate covers this case. The count was 192 in every configuration I tried (with and without Throttle, small buffers), so tightening does not threaten solvability.

findings.claim: Nothing checks the stated requirement 'flag the top of every ramp' (peak position). It is also missing from spec_properties. A peak train shifted away from the ramp tops passes.
findings.evidence: I inserted a blocks_delay of 40 samples (float) between Char To Float and peaks.dat. Every flag then sits half a period from a ramp top: flag_at_top_fraction is 0.0, against 1.0 for the reference. All 5 V6 checks still pass, with the same values as the reference. The checks only measure mean, max_abs and rms of peaks.dat, and none of the 6 spec_properties covers position. The reference output is fully deterministic (first flag at index 39, then every 80 samples), so position can be measured. Eval plan section 4.3 also says the V6 oracle 'compares the output ... with the reference on the same test inputs'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an f2p equal_prefix check on peaks against the reference indicator (1.0 at 39+80k, 0.0 elsewhere), for example skip 480, a few hundred to 1600 samples, max_offset 0. Add a 'peak_position' entry to spec_properties. Alternatively, reword the instruction to 'one detected peak per period' without promising position.

findings.claim: The instruction requires 'Keep the sawtooth, the Peak Detector2 settings ... as they are', but neither spec_properties nor the oracle covers this. Many changed settings pass. This confirms and extends the author's own open problem note.
findings.evidence: Each of these single edits to the reference passes all V6 checks: threshold factor 0.05, 0.3, 0.5 or 0.65 (outputs identical to the reference); alpha 0.001 (the example's original value) or 0.004 (average ripple 0.97 to 1.03); look-ahead 50, 55, 60 or 79 (or 43, see F1); Signal Source phase 1.0. Only factor 0.75 or more, look-ahead 40 or less or 81 or more, and the alpha 0.02 mutation fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the 'keep the Peak Detector2 settings' clause, since changes the oracle cannot see do not alter behaviour, or record it in spec_properties and review.notes as a structural constraint V6 does not check. The F1 and F2 fixes would catch the look-ahead and alpha changes that actually alter the outputs.

findings.claim: The p2p group does not mean 'pass-to-pass' for this item. The start graph fails at V3 and never runs, so the average.dat checks were never shown to hold in the starting flowgraph.
findings.evidence: In gates.json, start_fails gives first_failed V3 and v6_groups null. Eval plan section 4.3 and proposal section 5.2 define pass-to-pass as 'everything that worked in the starting flowgraph still works'. build.py's own comment says the p2p checks cover 'the path the fault did not touch', which is a different and weaker claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Note in the oracle check notes or spec_properties that for this V3 fault p2p means 'the branch the fault does not touch'. Better, show it: run the start graph with the faulty branch parked (detector out0 to a byte Null Sink) and confirm the two average.dat checks pass there.

item-quality.verdict:
Mostly holds up under adversarial review. I found no defect that would block the item, only the four findings above: one medium and three low.

What I checked and found sound:
- **Start state.** start.grc fails at V3 for exactly the stated reason. GRC reports that Source IO type "byte" does not match sink IO type "short", and that IO size 1 does not match IO size 2, on Peak Detector2 out(0) -> Short To Float.
- **Instruction.** A competent GNU Radio developer can solve it from the instruction plus the start graph. It names the files peaks.dat and average.dat, gives item type float, the indicator values 1.0/0.0, the sample rate, frequency, amplitude and offset, and the 0.1 s settle time. The fault symptom is described without naming the faulty block. No requirement is hidden.
- **Correct repairs are accepted.** These all reach V6: the three variants (I re-ran them 12 times in parallel with identical, deterministic results), an answer with literal numbers and samp_rate 48e3, absolute File Sink paths, and an answer that leaves the old Short To Float in the graph but disabled.
- **Wrong repairs are rejected.** A byte File Sink fed straight from the detector fails V6 because the observation point is missing. A leftover Short To Float that is enabled but unconnected fails V3. Char To Short followed by Short To Float at scale 1 (author's test) fails.
- **Reference behaviour.** The reference flags sample 39 of every 80-sample period, which is the top of the ramp: 205 peaks with spacing exactly 80. From 0.1 s the running average stays between 0.9806 and 1.0107.
- **Bookkeeping.** The split is right (blocks/peak_detector2.grc is a test seed and its sha256 matches). The canary appears only in task.json. The disjointness claim holds: no training-side spec mentions peak detection. L1 / repair / type_mismatch at V3 fits the proposal's definitions.

What is wrong:
- **F1 (medium).** spec_properties claims the average check catches a changed waveform. It does not: triangle and square waves pass, and so do 590 Hz and 605 Hz. So "Keep the sawtooth" is effectively unchecked.
- **F2 (low).** Changes to the Peak Detector2 settings pass, which the author already flagged. A flowgraph with no detector or sawtooth at all (a Vector Source pattern plus a Constant Source) also passes V6.
- **F3 (low).** The instruction says the average should "stay within 5 %" of 1.0, but the oracle checks only the upper bound and the mean.
- **F4 (low).** The average.dat checks are labelled p2p but are never shown to pass on the start state, since it fails at V3. I confirmed they do pass when only the faulty branch is neutralised, but the task does not record this.

My scratch files are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-09 (WSL). Nothing in the task directory was changed.

findings.claim: The spec_properties entry 'average_level' says its p2p mean check 'also catches a changed amplitude, offset or waveform'. The waveform part is false: if the 600 Hz sawtooth is swapped for a triangle or square wave with the same amplitude and offset, all five checks still pass. So the stated 'generates a 600 Hz sawtooth ... Keep the sawtooth' requirement is not checked for waveform shape. The only waveform mutant (a sine) is killed only because a sine is centred on 0.25 instead of about 1.0. The sawtooth frequency is also checked only coarsely: 590 Hz and 605 Hz pass.
findings.evidence: Ran ./gb ladder (via grcbench.tier_f.ladder.check with this task.json) on scratch files in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-09 (WSL home). k_tri.grc (waveform analog.GR_TRI_WAVE) reaches V6 and passes: peaks mean 0.0125, max_abs 1.0, rms 0.111803, average mean 1.000022, average max_abs 1.015033. k_sqr.grc (GR_SQR_WAVE) also passes: average mean 0.999979, max_abs 1.030023. k_saw590.grc passes (peak mean 0.012305, -1.6 %) and so does k_saw605.grc (0.01263). For comparison, amplitude 1.4 / 1.6 and offset 0.3 are correctly rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the checked_by text of 'average_level' to say that only changes that shift the mean (amplitude, offset, a sine centred on the offset) are caught, and that the sawtooth shape is not observable at peaks.dat or average.dat. Record this in review.notes. Optionally add a GR_TRI_WAVE mutant marked as a known survivor (the kill rate would stay at or above 0.9) so the limitation is visible in gates.json instead of being implied away.

findings.claim: The instruction's constraint 'Keep ... the Peak Detector2 settings' is not enforced by the oracle. Neither is the presence of the detector or the Signal Source. A flowgraph with no Peak Detector2 and no sawtooth at all passes V6. The author already flagged the settings part. The no-detector pass is new evidence of how loose the behavioural check is for this repair.
findings.evidence: These files all pass V6 with values identical or very close to the reference: k_factor03.grc (threshold_factor_rise 0.3), k_factor05.grc (0.5), k_alpha0001.grc, k_alpha0003.grc, k_look60.grc (look_ahead 60). k_look40 is rejected (peak mean 0.012891). b_cheat_no_detector.grc also passes all five checks. It is a Vector Source '[1.0]+[0.0]*79' (repeat) feeding the float File Sink peaks.dat, and a Constant Source 0.99 feeding average.dat: peaks mean 0.0125, max 1.0, rms 0.111803, average mean 0.99, max 0.99.
findings.suggested_fix: For a repair item this is unlikely to change real scores, so do not block the item. State in review.notes that 'keep' constraints on detector settings, the sawtooth and the presence of the detector are not verified by V6 and are covered only by the structural partial-credit score. If the harness later gains a structural assertion (block id present with given parameter values), add one for blocks_peak_detector2_fb (threshold_factor_rise 0.2, alpha 0.002, look_ahead 72).

findings.claim: The instruction states a two-sided requirement: the running average 'should stay within 5 % of the sawtooth's average level of 1.0'. The oracle checks only the mean (within 5 %) and the upper bound (max_abs ≤ 1.05). A running average that periodically sags below 0.95 while its mean stays at or above 0.95 would pass. The lower bound is stated but not checked.
findings.evidence: oracle.checks for point 'average' are mean expect 1.0 rel_tol 0.05, and max_abs max 1.05 (skip 4800). The spec_properties text of average_smooth says 'within 5 % of 1.0 (never above 1.05)', which admits that only the upper side is checked. The oracle feature set (oracles.py) has no min feature. In the reference run the minimum from sample 4800 is 0.9806, so the reference has ample margin.
findings.suggested_fix: Either reword the instruction to match what is checked (for example 'from 0.1 s after the start it should average within 5 % of 1.0 and never rise above 1.05'), or add a 'min' feature to oracles.py and a check of min ≥ 0.95 on average.dat after skip 4800.

findings.claim: The checks labelled 'p2p' on average.dat are never shown to pass on the starting flowgraph, because the start fails at V3 (gates.json start_fails.v6_groups is null). The eval plan defines pass-to-pass as 'everything that worked in the starting flowgraph still works'. As stored, the item gives no evidence that this branch 'worked' before the repair. If reports aggregate p2p failures as regressions, this item's p2p label is unsupported.
findings.evidence: gates.json: start_fails {first_failed: V3, v6_groups: null}. I neutralised only the faulty branch of start.grc: removed Short To Float and the peaks File Sink, and connected detector out0 to a byte Null Sink (c_start_minus_faulty_branch.grc). Result: f2p fails (the peaks observation is missing), both p2p checks pass (average mean 0.990651, max 1.010652). So the p2p label is defensible, but this is not recorded anywhere in the task.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to build.py (or to review.notes / fault) a recorded check that the p2p group passes on the start graph with only the faulted converter branch replaced by a Null Sink. Alternatively, document that for repair items failing at V3, p2p means 'the branch the fault does not touch'.
